config.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals

intro.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React form with accessible labels, error messages, and focus management to ensure it's usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. You'll learn core accessibility concepts like semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, and keyboard navigation. The main technologies involved are React components, JSX, and built-in HTML accessibility features. By the end, you'll understand how to make web applications more inclusive and compliant with accessibility standards.
intro.usecase: Accessibility (a11y) fundamentals are essential in any real-world React application that serves diverse users, including those with disabilities. For example, in e-commerce sites, accessible forms ensure screen readers can announce input labels and error messages during checkout, while accessible navigation menus allow keyboard users to browse product categories. Developers implement these a11y patterns in dashboards with proper ARIA roles for data tables, modals that trap focus for user interactions, and interactive filters with clear announcements for dynamic content updates, ensuring compliance and inclusive user experiences.

objectives: Apply semantic HTML elements to structure accessible React components
Configure ARIA attributes to enhance component accessibility for screen readers
Implement keyboard navigation handlers for interactive elements
Bind focus management to improve user navigation flow
Construct accessible form controls with proper labels and validation announcements
Integrate screen reader announcements for dynamic content updates
Manipulate component states to reflect accessibility status visually and programmatically

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and the useState hook from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty React fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns the fragment. This will be the main component of your application.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns an empty React fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your App component returns an empty React fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Remember to create a function named App that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state for accessibility mode
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'highContrastMode' with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Call useState(false) and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a boolean state variable
const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a state variable 'highContrastMode' initialized to false, ready to control accessibility features.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'highContrastMode' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with false as the initial value and naming the variable 'highContrastMode'.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState(false) inside the component and name the variable 'highContrastMode'.

steps.title: Define a toggle handler for accessibility mode
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named 'toggleHighContrast' that toggles the highContrastMode state value.
steps.hint: You can toggle a boolean state by setting it to the opposite of its current value using the state setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleHighContrast function is defined inside the App component that toggles the highContrastMode state between true and false.
successCriteria: The toggleHighContrast function is defined and uses setHighContrastMode to toggle the boolean state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggleHighContrast function properly toggles the boolean value using the state setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named toggleHighContrast that toggles the highContrastMode state.

steps.title: Add a main container with semantic HTML
steps.instruction: In your App component's return statement, replace the current return value with a <main> element that contains an <h1> heading with the text 'Accessibility Demo'.
steps.hint: The <main> element is a semantic HTML5 element that indicates the main content of the page. Place your heading inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a semantic <main> container with an <h1> heading inside.
successCriteria: The App component returns a <main> element containing an <h1> with the text 'Accessibility Demo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the <main> element and an <h1> heading with the exact text 'Accessibility Demo' inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should contain a <main> element with an <h1> heading inside. Check that you've replaced the previous return value completely.

steps.title: Add descriptive heading content
steps.instruction: Update the heading text to be more descriptive by changing it to 'Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals'.
steps.hint: Modify the text inside the <h1> tags to match the lesson title.
steps.expectedOutcome: The heading should now display 'Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals' as its content.
successCriteria: The <h1> element contains the exact text 'Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the heading text exactly matches 'Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading text doesn't match. Update the text inside the <h1> tags to 'Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals'.

steps.title: Add a toggle button with accessible label
steps.instruction: Inside your component, add a button element with an aria-label attribute set to 'Toggle high contrast mode' and wire its onClick event to the toggleHighContrast handler function.
steps.hint: Remember to define the toggleHighContrast function first if you haven't already. The button should have both aria-label and onClick attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with proper accessibility attributes will appear below the heading, ready to toggle the high contrast mode when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element includes both aria-label="Toggle high contrast mode" and onClick={toggleHighContrast} attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your button has both the aria-label attribute and the onClick handler wired to toggleHighContrast.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing required accessibility features. Check that you've added both aria-label and onClick attributes.

steps.title: Add dynamic button text based on state
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a button element with text that changes based on the highContrastMode state. Use a ternary operator to show 'Enable High Contrast' when highContrastMode is false, and 'Disable High Contrast' when it's true.
steps.hint: The button text should be set using a ternary operator: {highContrastMode ? 'Disable High Contrast' : 'Enable High Contrast'}
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will display 'Enable High Contrast' when highContrastMode is false, and 'Disable High Contrast' when it's true, providing clear feedback to users.
successCriteria: The button element includes a ternary operator that conditionally renders 'Enable High Contrast' or 'Disable High Contrast' based on the highContrastMode state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your button text changes correctly based on the highContrastMode state using a ternary operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button text should dynamically change based on the highContrastMode state. Try using a ternary operator to conditionally render different text.

steps.title: Apply conditional CSS class for high contrast
steps.instruction: Add a className attribute to the main element that conditionally applies a 'high-contrast' class when highContrastMode is true.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to set className to 'high-contrast' when highContrastMode is true, or an empty string when false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main element will have a dynamic className that adds 'high-contrast' when the toggle is enabled, allowing CSS to style it for better visual accessibility.
successCriteria: The main element includes a className attribute with a ternary expression that sets 'high-contrast' when highContrastMode is true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the className attribute uses a ternary operator to check highContrastMode.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction: you need to add a className attribute to the main element that conditionally applies 'high-contrast' based on the state.

steps.title: Add a descriptive paragraph with keyboard navigation info
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the button with text explaining keyboard navigation and tabindex for focus management.

successCriteria: A paragraph element with text about keyboard navigation and tabindex is added below the button.
